speaker: Doctor
text: How old is the newborn, and when did the bilious vomiting start? I need to know if the vomiting began within the first 24 hours of life or later, as this is a critical distinction.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, so I need to assess his abdominal status immediately. Is the abdomen distended or tender, and has he passed any meconium stools since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm if he has passed any meconium stool since birth, as failure to do so would strongly suggest intestinal atresia or Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
